setup.zh: 傍晚，山门外：舅舅在等你。夜里，大通铺上，孙二狗小声问：「明天那一块，你交不交？」
setup.en: Dusk outside the gate: your uncle is waiting. That night on the long bunk Sun Ergou whispers: "That one stone tomorrow — will you pay?"

recap.zh: 开山门那天傍晚：舅舅在山门外等你；夜里，他在泗水边的柳树底下埋了石蛋。大通铺上，马小宝跟老弟子嘀咕：新来的，一人一块。
recap.en: The evening the gate opened: your uncle waited outside; that night he buried Shidan under a willow by the Si. On the long bunk Ma Xiaobao muttered with the old disciples: the new ones, one stone each.

en: Outside the gate, your uncle looks up.
"That one stone tomorrow — will you pay?"

story.zh:
那天傍晚，新入门的弟子许出山门，跟送考的家里人说一句话，一炷香为限。执事把那面兵器架子抬上来了，小满取回了爷爷那张弓——第三排左数第七个，一个手指头也没人碰过——背在背上，跑出山门。

舅舅站在第三百级石阶边上，一见他便问：「……考上了？」小满道：「外门。」舅舅一把抓住了他的胳膊，这才看见他袖子上的血，脸一下子白了。小满道：「不是我的。」

他把林子里的事说了，说到「太华多远」，便说不下去了。舅舅半天没出声，末了道：「……我来。」

小满道：「舅舅，一百六十级那里，崖壁上刻满了字，都是在那一级上坐下过的人刻的。我替你走上来了。」舅舅把脸转过去，朝着泗水那边，过了好一会儿，才道：「……风大。」他拿袖子在脸上抹了一把，把小满背上那张弓扶正了，道：「回去吧。一炷香到了。」

山门合上以后，舅舅找到了廊下那个光脚的孩子，道：「济世堂缺个抓药跑腿的，管吃管住，一个月三百文。今夜先帮我挖个坑。」两个人去林子口讨了石蛋，在泗水边一棵柳树底下挖到半夜。舅舅不会刻字，拿炭在石头上写了两个字：石蛋。山脚客栈门口，马家的家丁把葛六的短刀折成了两截；葛六捡起那半截刀，往北边黑地里去了。

男弟子的大通铺上，鼾声一片。小满睡在最靠门的那张铺上，门缝里的风一夜往里灌。靠火盆那张最好的铺，是马小宝的。他的家丁不许在山上过夜，傍晚便下山去了，可天黑以后，另有两个进门三年的老弟子，嘴里带着酒气，蹲在他铺边上压着嗓子说话。小满只听清了几句：「……新来的一百多个，一人一块……」「……头一个月，三成归你……」「……那个杂灵根——」马小宝的声音：「他那块，我亲自收。」

小满旁边那张铺上，孙二狗也没睡，翻过身来，小声道：「明天那一块，你交不交？」小满道：「你呢？」孙二狗想了一想：「我交最小的那一块。」说完，翻回去，一会儿就打起了呼噜。
story.en:
Toward evening that day the new disciples were allowed out of the gate to say a word to the family who'd brought them, for the length of one stick of incense. The stewards had carried the weapons rack up; Xiaoman took his grandfather's bow back — third row, seventh from the left, not a finger laid on it — slung it on his back, and ran out of the gate.

His uncle stood by the three-hundredth step, and the moment he saw Xiaoman asked: "…Did you get in?" Xiaoman said, "Outer court." His uncle seized his arm — and only then saw the blood on his sleeve, and went white. Xiaoman said, "It isn't mine."

He told what had happened in the forest, and when he got to "how far to Taihua" he couldn't go on. His uncle said nothing for a long time; at last he said, "…I'll see to it."

Xiaoman said, "Uncle, at step one hundred and sixty the cliff wall is covered in writing — all carved by people who sat down on that step. I walked up for you." His uncle turned his face toward the Si, and after a good while said: "…Windy." He wiped his face with his sleeve, set the bow straight on Xiaoman's back, and said: "Go on back. The incense is out."

When the gate had closed, the uncle found the barefoot boy from the veranda. "The Jishi Hall needs a boy to fetch medicines and run errands. Board and lodging, three hundred coppers a month. Tonight, first, help me dig a hole." The two of them went to the forest's edge and asked for Shidan, and dug under a willow by the Si till midnight. The uncle couldn't carve; he wrote two words on a stone in charcoal: Shidan. At the door of the inn at the foot of the mountain, Ma servants snapped Ge Liu's short knife in two; Ge Liu picked up the half knife and went off north into the dark.

On the boys' long bunk, snoring everywhere. Xiaoman slept in the bed nearest the door, the draught through the crack blowing in all night. The best bed, by the brazier, was Ma Xiaobao's. His servants weren't allowed to stay the night on the mountain and had gone down at dusk; but after dark two old disciples three years in, breath smelling of wine, squatted by his bed talking low. Xiaoman caught only a few words: "…the hundred-odd new ones, one each…" "…first month, thirty in the hundred is yours…" "…that mixed root —" Ma Xiaobao's voice: "His, I'll collect myself."

On the bed beside Xiaoman, Sun Ergou wasn't asleep either; he turned over and whispered: "That one stone tomorrow — will you pay?" Xiaoman said, "Will you?" Sun Ergou thought a moment. "I'll pay the smallest one." And he turned back, and in a moment was snoring.

exits.means: pays the one stone to the common fund, keeps the peace for now

refuse.en: You have no spirit stones on you.

what.zh: 外门的「公中」：收了你一块灵石。
what.en: The outer court's "common fund": took one of your spirit stones.

story.zh:
小满把孙二狗那一句，在心里掂量了半夜。他掂量出来的是：一块灵石，买一个「懂事」，买马小宝一个月不来找麻烦。这笔账，眼下划得来。

第二天一早，饭堂门口，他从怀里摸出一块灵石，交了。马小宝掂了一掂，冲他笑，笑得跟他爹一模一样。

他心里却记了一笔：公中，一块。马小宝。
story.en:
Xiaoman weighed Sun Ergou's question half the night. What he weighed out was: one spirit stone buys "knowing his place", buys a month of Ma Xiaobao leaving him alone. For now, the sum comes out in his favour.

Next morning at the refectory door he took a spirit stone from his jacket and handed it over. Ma Xiaobao weighed it in his palm and grinned at him, a grin exactly like his father's.

But in his heart he entered a line: Common fund, one stone. Ma Xiaobao.

exits.means: refuses to pay the common fund

story.zh:
小满把孙二狗那一句，在心里掂量了半夜，掂量出来一个字：不。他把怀里的灵石一块一块放进他娘给的那个空钱袋里，叮，叮，叮。空钱袋里，头一回有了东西。

他知道往后会怎样：马小宝不会当着人的面动手，他会等。他爹就是这么收租的——先笑，再等，等你以为没事了，门就飞了。那就等。
story.en:
Xiaoman weighed Sun Ergou's question half the night, and weighed out one word: no. He put the spirit stones from his jacket one by one into the empty purse his mother had given him — *ting, ting, ting*. For the first time, the empty purse held something.

He knew what would come of it: Ma Xiaobao wouldn't lift a hand in front of people; he'd wait. That was how his father collected rent — grin first, then wait, wait till you think it's over, and then the door flies. Then let him wait.
